title: Episode 6: The Eighteen Parvas II: Virata, the War, and the Women

ending.reason: §2 ¶20 closes the Stri (eleventh) parva with its sloka count ("...seven hundred and seventy-five"). From §2 ¶13 at a target of 1080 s, `mbh episode breaks` ranks a mid-¶20 sentence first (1075 s, during the cremation) and this paragraph boundary second, a third of a point behind (1110 s). The paragraph boundary is between parvas, in narration, on a complete sentence. ¶19 (Sauptika) ends at 996 s, inside the window but well short of the target. ¶21 opens the Santi parva and, with the v6 sting, pushes the file past 20 minutes. Santi starts Ep 7.

lines.text: While the Pandavas, desirous of victory, were residing in the place called Upaplavya, Duryodhana and Arjuna both went at the same time to Vasudeva, and said,

lines.text: O ye first of men, a counsellor in myself who will not fight and one Akshauhini of troops, which of these shall I give to which of you?

lines.text: Blind to his own interests, the foolish Duryodhana asked for the troops; while Arjuna solicited Krishna as an unfighting counsellor.

lines.text: Then is described how, when the king of Madra was coming for the assistance of the Pandavas, Duryodhana, having deceived him on the way by presents and hospitality, induced him to grant a boon and then solicited his assistance in battle; how Salya, having passed his word to Duryodhana, went to the Pandavas and consoled them by reciting the history of Indra's victory (over Vritra).

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes the fall of the great Salya at the hands of Yudhishthira, the Just.
lines.tts_text: Then comes the fall of the great Salya at the hands of Yudhishthira, the Just.
lines.direction: reading the table of contents of a great epic; even, unhurried, each item distinct

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Here also is the death of Sakuni in battle at the hands of Sahadeva.
lines.tts_text: Here also is the death of Shakuni in battle at the hands of Sahadeva.
lines.direction: reading the table of contents of a great epic; even, unhurried, each item distinct

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Upon only a small remnant of the troops remaining alive after the immense slaughter, Duryodhana went to the lake and creating for himself room within its waters lay stretched there for some time.
lines.tts_text: Upon only a small remnant of the troops remaining alive after the immense slaughter, Duryodhana went to the lake and creating for himself room within its waters lay stretched there for some time.
lines.direction: reading the table of contents of a great epic; even, unhurried, each item distinct

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then is narrated the receipt of this intelligence by Bhima from the fowlers: then is narrated how, moved by the insulting speeches of the intelligent Yudhishthira, Duryodhana ever unable to bear affronts, came out of the waters.
lines.tts_text: Then is narrated the receipt of this intelligence by Bheema from the fowlers: then is narrated how, moved by the insulting speeches of the intelligent Yudhishthira, Duryodhana ever unable to bear affronts, came out of the waters.
lines.direction: reading the table of contents of a great epic; even, unhurried, each item distinct

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes the encounter with clubs, between Duryodhana and Bhima; then the arrival, at the time of such encounter, of Balarama: then is described the sacredness of the Saraswati; then the progress of the encounter with clubs; then the fracture of Duryodhana's thighs in battle by Bhima with (a terrific hurl of) his mace.
lines.tts_text: Then comes the encounter with clubs, between Duryodhana and Bheema; then the arrival, at the time of such encounter, of Balarama: then is described the sacredness of the Saraswathi; then the progress of the encounter with clubs; then the fracture of Duryodhana's thighs in battle by Bheema with his mace.
lines.direction: reading the table of contents of a great epic; even, unhurried, each item distinct

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: These all have been described in the wonderful ninth Parva.
lines.tts_text: These all have been described in the wonderful ninth Parva.
lines.direction: reading the table of contents of a great epic; even, unhurried, each item distinct

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: In this the number of sections is fifty-nine and the number of slokas composed by the great Vyasa—the spreader of the fame of the Kauravas—is three thousand, two hundred and twenty.
lines.tts_text: In this the number of sections is fifty-nine and the number of slokas composed by the great Vyasa—the spreader of the fame of the Kauravas—is three thousand, two hundred and twenty.
lines.direction: reading the table of contents of a great epic; even, unhurried, each item distinct

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then shall I describe the Parva called Sauptika of frightful incidents.
lines.tts_text: Then shall I describe the Parva called Sauptika of frightful incidents.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: On the Pandavas having gone away, the mighty charioteers, Kritavarman, Kripa, and the son of Drona, came to the field of battle in the evening and there saw king Duryodhana lying on the ground, his thighs broken, and himself covered with blood.
lines.tts_text: On the Pandavas having gone away, the mighty charioteers, Kritavarman, Kripaa, and the son of Drona, came to the field of battle in the evening and there saw king Duryodhana lying on the ground, his thighs broken, and himself covered with blood.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the great charioteer, the son of Drona, of terrible wrath, vowed,
lines.tts_text: Then the great charioteer, the son of Drona, of terrible wrath, vowed,
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: aswatthaman
lines.text: 'without killing all the Panchalas including Drishtadyumna, and the Pandavas also with all their allies, I will not take off armour.'
lines.tts_text: 'without killing all the Panchalas including Dhrishtadyumna, and the Pandavas also with all their allies, I will not take off armour.'
lines.direction: Aswatthaman's vow, low and hard; one sentence inside the summary

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Having spoken those words, the three warriors leaving Duryodhana's side entered the great forest just as the sun was setting.
lines.tts_text: Having spoken those words, the three warriors leaving Duryodhana's side entered the great forest just as the sun was setting.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: While sitting under a large banian tree in the night, they saw an owl killing numerous crows one after another.
lines.tts_text: While sitting under a large banian tree in the night, they saw an owl killing numerous crows one after another.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: At the sight of this, Aswatthaman, his heart full of rage at the thought of his father's fate, resolved to slay the slumbering Panchalas.
lines.tts_text: At the sight of this, Aswatthaman, his heart full of rage at the thought of his father's fate, resolved to slay the slumbering Panchalas.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And wending to the gate of the camp, he saw there a Rakshasa of frightful visage, his head reaching to the very heavens, guarding the entrance.
lines.tts_text: And wending to the gate of the camp, he saw there a Rakshasa of frightful visage, his head reaching to the very heavens, guarding the entrance.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And seeing that Rakshasa obstructing all his weapons, the son of Drona speedily pacified by worship the three-eyed Rudra.
lines.tts_text: And seeing that Rakshasa obstructing all his weapons, the son of Drona speedily pacified by worship the three-eyed Rudra.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And then accompanied by Kritavarman and Kripa he slew all the sons of Draupadi, all the Panchalas with Dhrishtadyumna and others, together with their relatives, slumbering unsuspectingly in the night.
lines.tts_text: And then accompanied by Kritavarman and Kripaa he slew all the sons of Drowpadee, all the Panchalas with Dhrishtadyumna and others, together with their relatives, slumbering unsuspectingly in the night.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: All perished on that fatal night except the five Pandavas and the great warrior Satyaki.
lines.tts_text: All perished on that fatal night except the five Pandavas and the great warrior Satyaki.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Those escaped owing to Krishna's counsels, then the charioteer of Dhrishtadyumna brought to the Pandavas intelligence of the slaughter of the slumbering Panchalas by the son of Drona.
lines.tts_text: Those escaped owing to Krishna's counsels, then the charioteer of Dhrishtadyumna brought to the Pandavas intelligence of the slaughter of the slumbering Panchalas by the son of Drona.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then Draupadi distressed at the death of her sons and brothers and father sat before her lords resolved to kill herself by fasting.
lines.tts_text: Then Drowpadee distressed at the death of her sons and brothers and father sat before her lords resolved to kill herself by fasting.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then Bhima of terrible prowess, moved by the words of Draupadi, resolved, to please her; and speedily taking up his mace followed in wrath the son of his preceptor in arms.
lines.tts_text: Then Bheema of terrible prowess, moved by the words of Drowpadee, resolved, to please her; and speedily taking up his mace followed in wrath the son of his preceptor in arms.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The son of Drona from fear of Bhimasena and impelled by the fates and moved also by anger discharged a celestial weapon saying,
lines.tts_text: The son of Drona from fear of Bhimasena and impelled by the fates and moved also by anger discharged a celestial weapon saying,
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: aswatthaman
lines.text: This is for the destruction of all the Pandavas'
lines.tts_text: This is for the destruction of all the Pandavas
lines.direction: the weapon, one short sentence

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: ; then Krishna saying.
lines.tts_text: Then Krishna saying,
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: krishna
lines.text: This shall not be
lines.tts_text: This shall not be
lines.direction: Krishna stopping the weapon; four words, firm and quiet

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: , neutralised Aswatthaman's speech.
lines.tts_text: Neutralised Aswatthaman's speech.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then Arjuna neutralised that weapon by one of his own.
lines.tts_text: Then Arjoona neutralised that weapon by one of his own.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Seeing the wicked Aswatthaman's destructive intentions, Dwaipayana and Krishna pronounced curses on him which the latter returned.
lines.tts_text: Seeing the wicked Aswatthaman's destructive intentions, Dwaipayana and Krishna pronounced curses on him which the latter returned.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Pandava then deprived the mighty warrior-in-chariot Aswatthaman, of the jewel on his head, and became exceedingly glad, and, boastful of their success, made a present of it to the sorrowing Draupadi.
lines.tts_text: Pandava then deprived the mighty warrior in chariot Aswatthaman, of the jewel on his head, and became exceedingly glad, and, boastful of their success, made a present of it to the sorrowing Drowpadee.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Thus the tenth Parva, called Sauptika, is recited.
lines.tts_text: Thus the tenth Parva, called Sauptika, is recited.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The great Vyasa hath composed this in eighteen sections.
lines.tts_text: The great Vyasa hath composed this in eighteen sections.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The number of slokas also composed (in this) by the great reciter of sacred truths is eight hundred and seventy.
lines.tts_text: The number of slokas also composed by the great reciter of sacred truths is eight hundred and seventy.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: In this Parva has been put together by the great Rishi the two Parvas called Sauptika and Aishika.
lines.tts_text: In this Parva has been put together by the great Rishee the two Parvas called Sauptika and Aishika.
lines.direction: the night attack, told evenly; no melodrama

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: After this hath been recited the highly pathetic Parva called Stri, Dhritarashtra of prophetic eye, afflicted at the death of his children, and moved by enmity towards Bhima, broke into pieces a statue of hard iron deftly placed before him by Krishna (as substitute of Bhima).
lines.tts_text: After this hath been recited the highly pathetic Parva called Stri, Dhritarashtra of prophetic eye, afflicted at the death of his children, and moved by enmity towards Bheema, broke into pieces a statue of hard iron deftly placed before him by Krishna.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then Vidura, removing the distressed Dhritarashtra's affection for worldly things by reasons pointing to final release, consoled that wise monarch.
lines.tts_text: Then Vidura, removing the distressed Dhritarashtra's affection for worldly things by reasons pointing to final release, consoled that wise monarch.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then hath been described the wending of the distressed Dhritarashtra accompanied by the ladies of his house to the field of battle of the Kauravas.
lines.tts_text: Then hath been described the wending of the distressed Dhritarashtra accompanied by the ladies of his house to the field of battle of the Kauravas.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Here follow the pathetic wailings of the wives of the slain heroes.
lines.tts_text: Here follow the pathetic wailings of the wives of the slain heroes.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the wrath of Gandhari and Dhritarashtra and their loss of consciousness.
lines.tts_text: Then the wrath of Gandhari and Dhritarashtra and their loss of consciousness.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the Kshatriya ladies saw those heroes,—their unreturning sons, brothers, and fathers,—lying dead on the field.
lines.tts_text: Then the Kshatriya ladies saw those heroes,—their unreturning sons, brothers, and fathers,—lying dead on the field.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the pacification by Krishna of the wrath of Gandhari distressed at the death of her sons and grandsons.
lines.tts_text: Then the pacification by Krishna of the wrath of Gandhari distressed at the death of her sons and grandsons.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the cremation of the bodies of the deceased Rajas with due rites by that monarch (Yudhishthira) of great wisdom and the foremost also of all virtuous men.
lines.tts_text: Then the cremation of the bodies of the deceased Rajas with due rites by that monarch of great wisdom and the foremost also of all virtuous men.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then upon the presentation of water of the manes of the deceased princes having commenced, the story of Kunti's acknowledgment of Karna as her son born in secret.
lines.tts_text: Then upon the presentation of water of the manes of the deceased princes having commenced, the story of Kunti's acknowledgment of Karna as her son born in secret.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Those have all been described by the great Rishi Vyasa in the highly pathetic eleventh Parva.
lines.tts_text: Those have all been described by the great Rishee Vyasa in the highly pathetic eleventh Parva.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Its perusal moveth every feeling heart with sorrow and even draweth tears from the eyes.
lines.tts_text: Its perusal moveth every feeling heart with sorrow and even draweth tears from the eyes.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The number of sections composed is twenty-seven.
lines.tts_text: The number of sections composed is twenty-seven.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The number of slokas is seven hundred and seventy-five.
lines.tts_text: The number of slokas is seven hundred and seventy-five.
lines.direction: the lament of the women; quiet, unhurried
